## Importing Data

```{r}
raw_data <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Diego150103/Enrollments_Data/refs/heads/main/merged_data.csv")

enrolment_data <- raw_data
```

```{r}
# 1) Create data frames with Fall and Spring census dates
fall_df <- data.frame(
  year = c(2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025),
  census_date = as.Date(c(
    "2020-09-08",  # Fall 2020
    "2021-09-07",  # Fall 2021
    "2022-09-06",  # Fall 2022
    "2023-09-05",  # Fall 2023
    "2024-09-04",  # Fall 2024
    "2025-09-03"   # Fall 2025
  ))
)

spring_df <- data.frame(
  year = c(2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025),
  census_date = as.Date(c(
    "2019-02-11",  # Spring 2019
    "2020-02-10",  # Spring 2020
    "2021-02-09",  # Spring 2021
    "2022-02-08",  # Spring 2022
    "2023-02-07",  # Spring 2023
    "2024-02-06",  # Spring 2024
    "2025-02-05"   # Spring 2025
  ))
)
```

## Data Cleaning

```{r}
clean_enrollment_data <- enrolment_data |>
  
  mutate(
    # Convert StartDate & EndDate from "m/d/yy" to Date objects
    StartDate = mdy(StartDate),
    EndDate   = mdy(EndDate),
    # Convert Timestamp from "m/d/yy hh:mm" to POSIXct
    Timestamp = mdy_hm(Timestamp)
  ) |>
    
  filter(
    # Keep only in-person MATH lectures, exclude Summer
    InstructionMode == "P",
    Component == "LEC",
    Subject == "MATH",
    !str_detect(TermDescr, regex("Summer", ignore_case = TRUE))
  ) |>
    
  select(
    Subject, CatalogNumber, Title, Section, StartDate, Timestamp, EnrollmentTotal, TermDescr
  ) |>
  
  mutate(
    # Convert these columns to factors
    Subject       = factor(Subject),
    Title         = factor(Title),
    CatalogNumber = factor(CatalogNumber),
    TermDescr     = factor(TermDescr)
  ) |>
  
  rename(
    # Rename columns for clarity
    subject              = Subject,
    catalog_number       = CatalogNumber,
    name_of_class        = Title,
    start_date           = StartDate,
    timestamp            = Timestamp,
    total_of_enrollments = EnrollmentTotal,
    term                 = TermDescr
  ) |>
  
  # 1) Extract 4-digit year from 'term' (e.g., "Fall 2024" → 2024)
  mutate(
    year = as.integer(str_extract(term, "\\d{4}")),
    # 2) Identify if it's Fall or Spring
    season = case_when(
      str_detect(term, "Fall")   ~ "Fall",
      str_detect(term, "Spring") ~ "Spring",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) |>
  
  # 3) Match each row's (season, year) to the correct census_date
  mutate(
    census_date = case_when(
      season == "Fall"   ~ fall_df$census_date[match(year, fall_df$year)],
      season == "Spring" ~ spring_df$census_date[match(year, spring_df$year)],
      TRUE               ~ as.Date(NA)
    )
  ) |>
  
  # 4) Remove any rows whose timestamp is after that term's census_date
  filter(timestamp <= census_date) |>
  
  # Finally, sort in ascending order by timestamp
  arrange(timestamp)
```

```{r}
#Convert enrollment data frame to a tible
clean_enrollment_data_tibble <- as_tibble(clean_enrollment_data)
```

```{r}
clean_enrollment_data2 <- clean_enrollment_data_tibble |>

  #Create a day-only column
  mutate(day_of_timestamp = as.Date(timestamp)) |>
  
  #For each course/day/section, keep the row with the earliest timestamp
  group_by(subject, catalog_number, name_of_class, term, start_date, day_of_timestamp, Section) |>
  filter(timestamp == min(timestamp)) |>
  # If multiple rows share the exact same timestamp, keep the one with max enrollment
  filter(total_of_enrollments == max(total_of_enrollments)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  
  #Sum across sections to get a single enrollment count per course/day
  group_by(subject, catalog_number, name_of_class, term, start_date, day_of_timestamp, census_date) |>
  summarize(
    total_of_enrollments = sum(total_of_enrollments, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  
  #Rename & sort
  rename(timestamp = day_of_timestamp) |>
  arrange(timestamp)
```

```{r}
# Suppose 'clean_enrollment_data2' is a data frame with:
#   subject, catalog_number, term, timestamp (POSIXct or Date),
#   total_of_enrollments, etc.

# 1) For each course+term, find earliest & latest daily timestamps,
#    converting them explicitly to Date
term_range <- clean_enrollment_data2 |>
  group_by(subject, catalog_number, term) |>
  summarize(
    earliest_date = as.Date(min(timestamp, na.rm = TRUE)),
    latest_date   = as.Date(max(timestamp, na.rm = TRUE)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# 2) For each course, define next_term_start as the day before the next term's earliest_date
term_range <- term_range |>
  group_by(subject, catalog_number) |>
  arrange(earliest_date) |>
  mutate(next_term_start = lead(earliest_date) - 1) |>
  ungroup()

# 3) Join 'next_term_start' back into clean_enrollment_data2
clean_enrollment_data2 <- clean_enrollment_data2 |>
  left_join(term_range |> select(subject, catalog_number, term, next_term_start),
            by = c("subject", "catalog_number", "term"))

# 4) Build a daily sequence for each (course+term)
fill_daily <- term_range |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(
    # If next_term_start is NA, fill only to that term's latest_date
    fill_end = ifelse(is.na(next_term_start), latest_date, next_term_start),
    # 'fill_end' might be numeric if the above ifelse returns NA or numeric
    # so we force it back to Date. Also ensure earliest_date is a Date.
    fill_end = as.Date(fill_end, origin = "1970-01-01"),
    earliest_date = as.Date(earliest_date, origin = "1970-01-01"),
    # Now create the daily sequence
    all_days = list(seq(from = earliest_date, to = fill_end, by = "day"))
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(subject, catalog_number, term, all_days) |>
  unnest(cols = c(all_days)) |>
  rename(timestamp = all_days)

# 5) Merge the expanded daily data with your original data
clean_enrollment_data3 <- fill_daily |>
  left_join(clean_enrollment_data2,
            by = c("subject", "catalog_number", "term", "timestamp")) |>
  # 6) For missing rows, fill total_of_enrollments with 0
  mutate(total_of_enrollments = coalesce(total_of_enrollments, 0)) |>
  arrange(subject, catalog_number, term, timestamp)
```

```{r}
top_six_bigger_class <- clean_enrollment_data3 |>
  filter(catalog_number %in% c("1010", "1401", "2830", "2411", "1060", "1110"))

# Filter data for every big class offered
calc1_data <- top_six_bigger_class |>
  filter(catalog_number == "1401")

math_for_liberal_data <- top_six_bigger_class |>
  filter(catalog_number == "1010")

intro_stats_data <- top_six_bigger_class |>
  filter(catalog_number == "2830")

calc2_data <- top_six_bigger_class |>
  filter(catalog_number == "2411")

finite_math <- top_six_bigger_class |>
  filter(catalog_number == "1060")

college_algebra_data <- top_six_bigger_class |>
  filter(catalog_number == "1110")
```

## Data Visualization

### Calculus I

```{r}
### Filter subsets
calc1_fall_data <- calc1_data |>
  filter(str_detect(term, "Fall"))

calc1_spring_data <- calc1_data |>
  filter(str_detect(term, "Spring"))

calc1_2024_data <- calc1_data |>
  filter(term == "Spring 2024" | term == "Fall 2024")

```

```{r}
# Plot all data for Calc I
calc1_all_graph <- calc1_data |>
  ggplot( aes(x = timestamp, y = total_of_enrollments)) +
    geom_area(fill="red", alpha=0.5) +
    geom_line(color="red") +
    labs(
      title = "Enrollment Over Time for Calculus I (MATH 1401)",
      x = "Date",
      y = "Enrollment Total"
    ) +
    theme_minimal()

calc1_all_graph <- ggplotly(calc1_all_graph)
calc1_all_graph

top_six_spring_plotly <- ggplotly(top_six_spring_plot)
top_six_spring_plotly


### Plot 2024 (Spring + Fall)
top_six_2024_plot <- top_six_2024_data |>
  ggplot(aes(x = timestamp, y = total_of_enrollments, color = catalog_number)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    title = "2024 Enrollment Trends for Top 6 MATH Classes",
    x = "Date",
    y = "Enrollment Total",
    color = "Catalog Number"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

top_six_2024_plotly <- ggplotly(top_six_2024_plot)
top_six_2024_plotly
```

### ARIMA TRY

```{r}
useful_calc1_enrollment_data <- calc1_data |>
  mutate(term_year = as.integer(str_extract(term, "\\d{4}"))) %>%
  filter(term_year > 2021 | (term_year == 2021 & str_detect(term, regex("Fall", ignore_case = TRUE)))) %>%
  select(-term_year)
```

```{r}
arima_calc <- ts(useful_calc1_enrollment_data$total_of_enrollments, frequency = 150)

model_arima_calc <- auto.arima(arima_calc, seasonal = T)

summary(model_arima_calc)
```

```{r}
prediction <- forecast(model_arima_calc, h = 200)

plot(prediction, main = "SARIMA Forecast of Enrollment", ylab = "Enrollment", xlab = "Time")
```
